title: John Adams: 291 Years Ago Today, the Lawyer Who Defended the Enemy

lines: He defended the soldiers who shot his neighbors.
Who changed the world today? October 30.
Who changed the world today? October thirtieth.
291 years ago today, a boy was born in Massachusetts:
Two hundred ninety-one years ago today, a boy was born in Massachusetts:
John Adams.

scenes.chapter: Chapter 1  The case no one would take
lines: On March 5, 1770, British soldiers fired into a Boston crowd,
On March fifth, seventeen seventy, British soldiers fired into a Boston crowd,
killing five people.
The city was furious. No lawyer would defend them.
But a young lawyer named John Adams took the case.
He believed everyone deserves a fair trial.
He told the jury: facts are stubborn things.
In the end, the captain and six of the eight soldiers were acquitted.
In Congress, Adams pushed hard for independence.
He chose young Thomas Jefferson to write the Declaration,
and fought for it on the floor.
On July 4, 1776, the Declaration was adopted.
On July fourth, seventeen seventy-six, the Declaration was adopted.

scenes.chapter: Chapter 3  First in the White House
lines: In 1797, he became America's second president,
In seventeen ninety-seven, he became America's second president,
and the first to live in the White House.
Later, he and Jefferson fell out over politics.
In 1812, Adams wrote first,
In eighteen twelve, Adams wrote first,
and their letters went on for fourteen years.
On July 4, 1826, fifty years after the Declaration,
On July fourth, eighteen twenty-six, fifty years after the Declaration,
Adams, ninety, said: Thomas Jefferson survives.
He didn't know that Jefferson had died a few hours earlier.
The Massachusetts Constitution he drafted in 1780
The Massachusetts Constitution he drafted in seventeen eighty
is still the oldest working constitution in the world.
His question for you:
if a whole city hated someone,
would you still stand up for their fair trial?
This is Who Changed the World Today,
and on October 30, we remember John Adams.
